newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Feb housing starts rise 9.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Feb housing starts rise 9.6 pct.

text.p: Canadian housing starts rose by 9.6 percent in February to a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR) of 158,900 units from 145,000 units in January, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Monday.
A Reuter survey of economists had forecast housing starts would show a rise of 143,200 units in February.
Actual housing starts rose to 7,394 in February from 7,247 the month before. The SAAR is a monthly figure adjusted to remove normal seasonal variation and multiplied by 12.

The housing corporation said momentum in the single
detached market picked up, with the February number being the best since April 1990.

"Lower mortage rates, together with favorable employment, income, house price and low inventory conditions boosted new home construction, particularly that geared to home ownership," said senior CMHC economist Michel Lawrence.
